title: A step towards personalized sports nutrition: carbohydrate intake during exercise
population: Endurance athletes; guideline proposal on carbohydrate intake during exercise by duration and intensity
findings: For ~1 h events, a mouth rinse or small amounts of carbohydrate can improve performance.
A single carbohydrate source can be oxidised at up to ~60 g/h; this is the recommendation for more prolonged exercise (2-3 h).
For ultra-endurance events the recommendation is higher, ~90 g/h, and must be multiple transportable carbohydrates to allow high oxidation and prevent intestinal accumulation.

Source may be liquid, semisolid or solid; recommendations may be adjusted downward when absolute exercise intensity (and CHO oxidation) is low; advice is independent of body weight and training status.
limitations: Narrative guideline proposal; the ~90 g/h ultra figure is an extrapolation from oxidation physiology, not tested in ultras, and sits above Tiller 2019's 30-50 g/h; does not address individual gut tolerance.
implications: Tiers by duration: ~1 h small amounts/rinse; 2-3 h up to ~60 g/h single source; > ~2.5 h up to ~90 g/h only as multiple transportable carbohydrates.
Scale down when absolute intensity is low (e.g. slow mountain ultra or walking), not by body mass.
For 100 mi use the Tiller 30-50 g/h baseline plus the gut-training pathway to 60-90 g/h only when tolerated.

verification.notes: Crossref match; all findings in the Europe PMC abstract. Removed the researcher's '1-2 h 30 g/h' and '2:1 glucose:fructose' tier details and the 'industry ties' claim because they are not in the abstract and were not verified.
